official.description_text:
Researcher in organic electrosynthesis
Apply for position
KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Engineering Sciences in Chemistry, Biotechnology and Health
Job description
We seek a driven research engineer to carry out method development in organic electrosynthesis in the research group of Associate Professor Helena Lundberg at the Department of Chemistry. Administrative tasks are also important aspects of the work.
Qualifications
Requirements
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree in the subject area.
Documented ability to work independently as well as collaborative in a group.
Documented scientific skills in method development for organic electrosynthesis.
The ability to skillfully communicate in English, verbally and in writing, as it is required in the daily work.
Personal qualities
As a person, you possess academic skills (both practical laboratory skills and theoretical), you are communicative and show good collaboration skills. Furthermore, you are independent in your work and have good pedagogical skills.
Preferred qualifications
Experience of administering chemical inventory.
Awareness of diversity and equal treatment policies and practices.
Great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Join us at KTH
KTH shapes the future through education, research and innovation. As a leading international technical university, we play an active role in advancing the transition towards a sustainable society. At KTH, you have the opportunity to grow and develop in a creative and dynamic environment, with good working conditions and attractive benefits. Equality, diversity and equal opportunities are essential to quality and form an integral part of KTH’s core values as a university and public authority.
Learn more about our benefits and what it's like to work and grow at KTH
.
Trade union representatives

trade union representatives

To apply for the position
Log into KTH's recruitment system in order to apply for this position. You are responsible to ensure that your application is complete according to the instructions in the ad.
The application must include:
CV including relevant professional experience and knowledge where the points under “Requirements” are clearly accounted for.
Copy of diplomas and grades from your previous university studies. Translations into English or Swedish is needed if the original documents have not been issued in any of these languages.
Written documentation that support the points under “Requirements” where documentation is asked for.
Brief account of why you want to conduct research, your academic interests and how they relate to your previous studies and future goals (max two pages long).
Your complete application must be received by KTH no later than the last day of application, midnight CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time).
About the employment
The employment is valid for a limited time according to the agreement - for up to 4 months, with access according to agreement.
Other information
For
information about processing of personal data
in the recruitment process.
It may be the case that a position at KTH is classified as a security-sensitive role in accordance with the Protective Security Act (2018:585). If this applies to the specific position, a security clearance will be conducted for the applicant in accordance with the same law with the applicant's consent. In such cases, a prerequisite for employment is that the applicant is approved following the security clearance.
We firmly decline all contact with staffing and recruitment agencies and job ad salespersons.

ai.summary: Limited-term research engineer position (up to 4 months) in organic electrosynthesis method development at KTH's Department of Chemistry, led by Associate Professor Helena Lundberg. Role includes both research and administrative responsibilities.

thematic_fit.rationale: No thematic overlap whatsoever. This is organic chemistry research focused on synthetic method development. The researcher's domains are human-centred XR, immersive systems, spatial cognition, and learning—completely orthogonal to chemical synthesis.

methodological_fit.rationale: No methodological fit. The role demands documented skills in organic electrosynthesis method development and laboratory chemistry practice. The researcher's methodologies are entirely centred on XR system design, user studies, and empirical evaluation of human factors. There is no transferable methodological foundation.

growth_value.rationale: This position offers zero growth value toward the researcher's stated capabilities and long-term identity. It does not develop XR systems thinking, immersive interaction design, user research methods, spatial cognition understanding, or any other dimension aligned with the researcher's target identity.

strategic_value.rationale: While KTH is in a preferred country (Sweden), the specific lab and role are strategically irrelevant. The position is also time-limited (4 months maximum), offering no stable foundation for a research trajectory. The connection to the researcher's target institutions and research groups is nil.

eligibility_flags: Requires doctoral degree in a chemistry-related discipline; researcher holds MSc in Multimedia/HCI
Posting demands 'documented scientific skills in method development for organic electrosynthesis'—researcher has no chemistry background or publications in this area
Position explicitly requires practical laboratory chemistry skills; researcher's skillset is entirely computational/systems design and user-facing research
risks: Complete domain mismatch: chemistry/organic synthesis vs. human-centred XR research
Researcher lacks the foundational qualification (chemistry PhD or equivalent) and would not meet eligibility criteria
Extremely short contract (up to 4 months) offers no meaningful research continuity or career development
Administrative responsibilities may distract from meaningful research contributions
Accepting this role would signal a departure from the researcher's established research identity and could confuse future applications to HCI/XR positions
